newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rio Tinto says invests in gypsum deposit.
newsitem.headline: Rio Tinto says invests in gypsum deposit.

text.p: Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd, formerly Anglo-Australian group RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, said on Tuesday its 64.9 percent-owned Dampier Salt Ltd subsidiary invested A$27 million in developing a massive gypsum deposit at Lake MacLeod, Western Australia.
A major new gypsum export project is being commissioned for Asian markets on the lake, where Dampier Salt already produces one million tonnes of chemical salt annually for export to Asia, it said.

"The plant will produce high quality gypsum, initially at an annual rate of 1.5 million tonnes -- a fraction of its total reserves -- for sale to Japan, Taiwan, South Korea and Indonesia," Rio Tinto said.
Gypsum from Lake McLeod will take up the slack in the Japanese market, where the tradional supplier, Thailand is diverting more of its production to its own domestic market, the company said.
Lake MacLeod, north of Carnarvon, is 110 km long and up to 40 km wide, covered by two metres of gypsum, with salt below it.
Reserves are estimated at 3.5 billion tonnes of gypsum on the lake, with an initial mining plan of 300 million tonnes.
The product will be shipped from Cape Cuvier, the existing salt export port, Rio Tinto said.

Deliveries are to start later this year following the signing of long-term supply contracts with major wallboard and cement manufacturers in Japan, Western Australia Resources Development Minister Colin Barnett said at the official opening ceremony for the project on Tuesday.
Gypsum is used in the making of plasterboard and other building products.
